subject: Request: Deterministic throughput carveout for Dedicated pool (Letterbox AI)
messages:
From: Jordan Harper <jordan@letterbox.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@letterbox.ai
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Deterministic throughput carveout for Dedicated pool

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profiles looked promising. We’re evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production rollout of our conversational moderation feature and have one open item before procurement: deterministic throughput for a reserved GPU pool during peak inference windows.

Specific ask:
- A soft guarantee of X tokens/sec across a pinned subset of reserved GPUs (we can tolerate short 30–60s microbursts, but need sustained throughput for 30-minute windows during business-critical periods).
- Clarity on queueing behavior when tenant demand spikes — do we preempt or enqueue, and what crediting/compensation is available for preemptions?
- A clear definition of what counts as an SLA breach (percentile, measurement window) and proposed credit amounts.

I’ve attached a short CSV with our observed traffic shape (letterbox_request_metrics.csv) and a draft amendment (Letterbox_SLA_Requested_Amendment_v1.pdf) that our procurement team prefers as a starting point.

Can your team propose language/operational guarantees we can review with legal? We’d like to finalize terms before the end of June to align with our internal release.

Appreciate any flexibility — happy to jump on a call if it helps align definitions.

Best,
Jordan Harper
Head of Infrastructure
Letterbox AI

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Harper <jordan@letterbox.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Deterministic throughput carveout for Dedicated pool

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear note and the artifacts, they’re super helpful. Quick read-through notes below and a request for one additional data point:

High-level: we can support a carveout with deterministic throughput semantics, but the operational model differs depending on how rigid you need the guarantee and the size of the pinned pool. We typically offer:
- Soft deterministic window: guaranteed sustained throughput for X minutes with a 95th percentile tail measured over 24h windows (crediting model applies on violations).
- Hard isolation (larger reserved fleet): stronger guarantees but requires upfront capacity commit and adoption of our dedicated concurrency controls.

Questions / ask from our side:
- In your CSV you’ve included 1s and 1m aggregates. Can you add a sample 5–15 minute aggregate for peak windows and call out the maximum sustained token/sec you need for 30-min windows? That helps us map to a reserved node count.

Internal next steps: I’m looping in Ben (sales lead) and Laura (contracts/product counsel) to draft an amendment that balances your needs and our platform constraints. Ben — can you draft a workable credit schedule and an operational playbook (eviction vs enqueue behavior, monitoring thresholds) we can offer? Laura — please flag any legal concerns in the attached draft.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk through the numbers unless you prefer a doc-based iteration first.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Harper <jordan@letterbox.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Deterministic throughput carveout for Dedicated pool

Jordan / Olga / Laura —

Thanks — did a quick sizing exercise against the CSV. Two proposal options below that trade cost vs. determinism:

Option A — Soft-deterministic (lower cost, faster provisioning)
- Reserved pool sized to meet requested sustained token/sec for 30-minute windows at 95% of observed peaks.
- Queueing behavior: incoming requests beyond reserved capacity will be enqueued; eviction only if tenant exceeds pinned concurrency limit. Short microbursts (<=60s) will be absorbed by burst headroom but not guaranteed.
- SLA measurement: 99th percentile latency for generation tail and sustained throughput measured in 30-minute windows. Breach credit: 5% monthly usage credit per confirmed 30-minute window breach (capped at 30% monthly).

Option B — Isolation-backed deterministic (higher cost, stronger guarantee)
- Larger dedicated node set with strict tenant isolation and pinned slots.
- Preemption: none for the pinned slots during the contracted windows. Other tenants may be preempted.
- SLA measurement: deterministic throughput guaranteed at the contracted token/sec over rolling 30-minute windows with an operational SLO of 99.5%. Breach credit: 10% monthly usage credit per confirmed 30-minute window breach (capped at 50% monthly).

Operational playbook draft (summary):
- Monitoring: we’ll emit token/sec and tail latency metrics to your telemetry (or provide read-only dashboard).
- Incident: if sustained throughput drops below contracted levels for >30 minutes, Redwood runbook triggers: immediate mitigation (scale within dedicated pool / failover to standby nodes), automated paging to support rotation, and post-incident credit evaluation.
- Credit verification: we use server-side metrics and cross-check with your sample telemetry; a joint review window of 7 business days for confirmation.

Next steps: Jordan — can you confirm which option you’d prefer and the committed months/annual term? Also please send the 5–15m aggregates Olga requested. We can then translate Option B sizing into a draft amendment document for legal.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Lead — Dedicated Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Harper <jordan@letterbox.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, contracts@letterbox.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Deterministic throughput carveout for Dedicated pool

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Ben’s two-option approach matches what I’d expect; to keep procurement moving I recommend the following interim plan:

1) Start with Option A for the initial 3-month committed term (lower ramp cost), with a scheduled conversion to Option B if your observed 30-day peak > 85% of the Option A capacity for two consecutive weeks.
2) We’ll include a carveout window in the amendment: 0300–0600 UTC daily (your identified heavy batch window) where preemption is limited and burst headroom is allocated. Outside that window we keep standard reserved behavior.
3) Credit schedule: align to Ben’s draft but cap immediate single-window credits at 7.5% to reduce billing noise; escalate to Laura for any language changes.

Attached: Redwood_proposed_SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf (attachment stub). I’ll open a DocuSign envelope with the term-sheet after you confirm the ramp term and the committed months.

If that’s agreeable Jordan, I’ll get the term-sheet into DocuSign by Thursday. Otherwise, we can discuss specifics on a quick call.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0193
